clue.text: A subject calling for deep consideration

definitions.text: A subject calling for deep consideration

parts.words: A subject calling for deep consideration
parts.note: deep is read literally as the ocean depths, so the subject is the scientific study of the seas

explanation.surface: Some topic demands profound thought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deep consideration' looks like serious thinking; it is the study of the deep, the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The science of the oceans is literally an academic field concerned with the deep.

clue.text: Not all furniture-removers etc, expect to be tipped too much

definitions.text: expect to be tipped too much

indicators.note: Not all says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Removal men and the like anticipate generous gratuities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not all' takes only part of 'removers etc', reading across the word break. 'Tipped too much' plays on gratuities but means knocked over, upset.
explanation.definitionFit: To overturn something is to tip it over too far, the old sense of upsetting a vessel or cart.

clue.text: Order in French, do!

parts.note: the French word for in is en
to do something is to act

explanation.surface: A command given in French: get on with it!
explanation.definitionFit: To decree a law or rule is to command it formally, so ordering is a synonym.

clue.text: All is fine for the makers of personal grooming aids

indicators.note: the phrase All is fine is what these items are made from, by rearranging its letters

explanation.surface: Everything is fine for the manufacturers of beauty products.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The makers of' looks like manufacturers; it signals that ALL IS FINE is rearranged to make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Small abrasive tools for shaping fingernails are typical items in a manicure kit.

clue.text: A song sung for joy?

parts.note: the word for a part-song for unaccompanied voices is also the word for delight, so it is a song named after joy

explanation.surface: A tune performed out of happiness.
explanation.walkthrough: In English music this is an unaccompanied part-song for three or more voices; the same word means merriment.
explanation.definitionFit: An old English part-song shares its name with merriment or high spirits.

clue.text: Unqualified sailing man thus stuck on the mud

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor
so means thus
lute is a clay or cement used to seal joints, a kind of mud

explanation.surface: A yachtsman, unconditionally beached, is stuck fast in the mire.
explanation.walkthrough: LUTE here is not the instrument but a sealing clay or cement used by chemists and builders.
explanation.definitionFit: Absolute power or trust is complete and without any reservation or condition.

clue.text: An organ requires the temperature to be about right

indicators.note: the temperature word goes around, about, the letter for right

parts.note: heat is temperature

explanation.surface: An instrument needs its temperature correctly adjusted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organ' suggests the musical instrument; it is the body's blood pump.
explanation.definitionFit: The pump in the chest is one of the body's vital organs.

clue.text: A way to encourage production of fish

parts.note: ST, street, is a way
to urge on is to encourage

explanation.surface: A method of boosting fish farming output.
explanation.definitionFit: This large river fish is the source of caviar.

clue.text: Fruit for a royal house

explanation.surface: A fruit for the royals.
explanation.definitionFit: A citrus fruit, and the Dutch royal line of William of Orange, who also ruled Britain.

clue.text: They question cut-back by underground workers

indicators.note: back says the word for cut is read in reverse

parts.note: to axe is to cut
miners work below ground

explanation.surface: Interrogators query the cutbacks made by pitmen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut-back' reads as one word for a reduction; split it, and 'back' turns AXE into EXA.
explanation.definitionFit: Inspectors who set tests or interrogate witnesses ask the questions.

clue.text: A teacher losing his head and making a bloomer

indicators.note: the first letter of the teacher word is dropped

parts.note: a schoolmaster is a teacher

explanation.surface: A schoolmaster is beheaded and commits a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making a bloomer' suggests a mistake; a bloomer here is a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: A daisy-like garden flower is something that blooms.

clue.text: Display well started

explanation.surface: Put on a good show that began nicely.
explanation.definitionFit: To enhance by contrast, showing something to advantage; and to begin a journey.

clue.text: It makes things smoother for the home club

parts.note: a flat is a home
an iron is a golf club

explanation.surface: A tool for smoothing at the domestic golf club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Club' suggests a society; it is the golf club.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned smoothing iron heated on the stove pressed creases out of clothes.

clue.text: Play bagatelle?

explanation.surface: Perform the game of bar billiards?
explanation.definitionFit: To toy with something; and a thing of little value or importance.

clue.text: Love of imagery when it is adroitly handled

indicators.note: handled suggests the letters of adroitly are manipulated into a new order

explanation.surface: Fondness for pictures, when it is deftly managed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Imagery' looks like poetic language; here it is images worshipped, idols.
explanation.definitionFit: Worship of graven images is excessive devotion to idols.

clue.text: Impressed by Eastern flight

parts.note: to be impressed is to be stamped, as on wax

explanation.surface: Struck by an oriental escape.
explanation.definitionFit: A panicked rush of a herd is a headlong flight.

clue.text: Wholly sound, if antiquated

explanation.surface: Completely solid, though old-fashioned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wholly sound' is read as what sounds like 'wholly': holey, full of holes, as a garment eaten by moths.
explanation.definitionFit: Full of holes made by clothes moths, said aloud as wholly; and figuratively worn out and outdated.

clue.text: Governor has to settle on a worker, though in some doubt

parts.note: HE, His Excellency, is a governor's title
to settle is to sit
an ant is a worker

explanation.surface: The governor must sit on an employee, though uncertain.
explanation.walkthrough: HE stands for His Excellency, the style of a colonial governor or ambassador.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is unsure and holds back is wavering and tentative.

clue.text: An enclosed place might be costlier

indicators.note: might be says the letters of costlier could become another word

explanation.surface: A walled place could be more expensive.
explanation.definitionFit: A covered walkway around a monastery courtyard is an enclosed retreat.

clue.text: A youngster with a short answer for people

parts.note: a cub is a youngster
ans is a short form of answer

explanation.surface: A child gives a curt reply for everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: Natives of a Caribbean island nation are a people.

clue.text: A stimulant, though that's not stressed

parts.note: a tonic is a stimulant

explanation.surface: A pick-me-up, though that one is not stressful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not stressed' suggests calm; in phonetics it means an unaccented syllable.
explanation.definitionFit: In speech, a syllable without accent is unstressed.

clue.text: Clot gets unceremonious dismissal with a pound

parts.note: conge is an abrupt dismissal
L is the abbreviation for pound, from libra

explanation.surface: A fool is sacked abruptly along with a pound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clot' looks like a noun for an idiot; it is the verb, to thicken.
explanation.definitionFit: To clot is to set or solidify from a liquid state.

clue.text: The family after support's on guard

indicators.note: after puts the family word behind the support word

parts.note: support's is supports, and to support is to bear
kin is family

explanation.surface: The relatives behind the backing are on watch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On guard' suggests alert; it means worn on a guardsman, the tall fur hat of British guards regiments.
explanation.definitionFit: The tall black fur cap is worn by British foot guards on sentry duty.

clue.text: Labour needs to retain about fifty

indicators.note: about says the retain word goes around the fifty letter

parts.note: to save is to retain
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: The Labour Party must hold on to around fifty seats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour' looks like the British political party; it is the verb, toil.
explanation.definitionFit: To toil hard like a drudge is to work as a bondsman would.

clue.text: Start wearing a jacket

parts.note: a jerk is a sudden start
in means wearing, as in dressed in

explanation.surface: Begin putting on a coat.
explanation.definitionFit: A close-fitting sleeveless coat is a kind of short jacket.

clue.text: A drab colour suits some men all the same

definitions.text: A drab colour suits some men all the same

parts.words: A drab colour suits some men all the same
parts.note: the dull brownish shade is the colour of uniforms, suits that make soldiers all the same

explanation.surface: A dull shade flatters certain men nonetheless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suits' looks like a verb meaning flatters; it is the noun, the uniforms soldiers wear, and 'all the same' means uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: The dull yellow-brown cloth is that of army uniforms.

clue.text: Game reserves

explanation.surface: Game reserves.
explanation.definitionFit: A cue sport like billiards; and a shared fund or stock of resources.

clue.text: The new man or woman

indicators.note: new says the letters of man or are made into a fresh word

explanation.surface: The modern man or woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name, as in Bellini's opera heroine, so a woman.

clue.text: The American army's revolutionary command

parts.note: revolutionary is read as turning round, so the order is the US drill command to turn to the rear

explanation.surface: An order from the forces of the American Revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' suggests the War of Independence; it means turning about, the US version of the British about turn.
explanation.definitionFit: The drill order to turn and face the opposite way is the US term for an about turn.

clue.text: Snipe a little, annoying as it may be

indicators.note: as it may be suggests the letters of snipe a little can be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: Take small potshots, irritating though that is.
explanation.definitionFit: Something troublesome and pernicious, like a plague, is figuratively irritating.
